title: Find My Mouse not working right on Multi-Monitor setup

judgment.rationale: The report is already specific enough for a maintainer-side reproduction pass: it gives a short non-primary-monitor repro and a concrete mispositioned spotlight symptom.
evidence: The issue gives a four-step repro using default Find My Mouse settings and moving the pointer to the second monitor.
The actual behavior is precise: the darkened screen effect starts near the cursor but the spotlight circle ends up back on the main monitor instead of the monitor containing the cursor.
The live issue has no comments asking for clarification, suggesting the first missing step is internal reproduction rather than more author restatement.
FindMyMouse.cpp covers the entire virtual screen in one overlay window and converts cursor position with ScreenToClient, which is compatible with cross-monitor coordinate/positioning bugs.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the spotlight drift on a multi-monitor setup and inspect the virtual-screen coordinate path before choosing a fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: The next bounded step is a maintainer reproduction check; the source suggests where to look, but not enough to lock a specific fix yet.

issue_context.summary: Find My Mouse reportedly misplaces its spotlight on the primary monitor when activated from a secondary monitor. The public repro is already concise enough for an internal reproduction pass.
known_information: The issue targets Mouse Utilities / Find My Mouse on PowerToys 0.100.2.
The reporter uses default settings and triggers the utility with the left Ctrl double-tap while the cursor is on the second monitor.
The actual symptom is not a total failure; the screen darkens but the spotlight circle ends up on the main monitor instead of following the pointer on the second monitor.
There are no comments, attachments, or linked fixes in the live issue.
inferences: The utility is probably activating correctly, but using the wrong translated position or wrong root coordinate space for non-primary monitors.
Because the repro is already tight and monitor-specific, maintainer reproduction is cheaper than sending a generic evidence request back to the reporter.
issue_context.analysis: This fits the 'reproducible' bucket better than 'needs information'. The issue already names the module, trigger, and user-visible failure. Source review shows a plausible virtual-screen coordinate path to instrument, but lightweight triage should stop at a maintainer reproduction action rather than inventing a full fix design.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue body and confirmed there are no public follow-up comments or linked PRs.
Inspected FindMyMouse.cpp around StartSonar and OnMouseTimer.
Confirmed the module creates one virtual-screen-sized overlay window and converts the global cursor position to client coordinates with ScreenToClient before moving the spotlight.

actions.label: Reproduce secondary-monitor spotlight drift
actions.note: Validate the reported non-primary-monitor positioning failure before selecting a code fix.

reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.100.2 or a nearby build with default Find My Mouse settings.
prerequisites: A Windows machine with at least two monitors arranged side-by-side.
Find My Mouse enabled with the default left-Ctrl-double-tap activation.
steps: Move the pointer to a secondary monitor and leave it stationary there.
Trigger Find My Mouse with the configured double-left-Ctrl activation.
Observe whether the darkened overlay and spotlight center remain on the monitor currently containing the pointer.
Repeat with different monitor arrangements or scaling if needed to confirm whether the spotlight snaps back toward the primary monitor.
reproduce.expected_result: The spotlight should stay centered on the actual cursor position even when the cursor is on a non-primary monitor.
